title: JEE Main 2026 · 23 Jan · Shift 1 (recreated)

qs.stem: A rectangle is formed by the lines x = 0, y = 0, x = 3 and y = 4. Let the line L be perpendicular to 3x + y + 6 = 0 and divide the area of the rectangle into two equal parts. Then the distance of the point (1/2, −5) from the line L is equal to :
steps: A line perpendicular to 3x + y + 6 = 0 has the form x − 3y + c = 0.
To halve the rectangle's area it must pass through the centre (3/2, 2): 3/2 − 6 + c = 0, so c = 9/2.
Distance of (1/2, −5): |1/2 + 15 + 9/2|/√10 = 20/√10 = 2√10.

qs.stem: Let α and β respectively be the maximum and the minimum values of the function f(θ) = 4(sin<sup>4</sup>(7π/2 − θ) + sin<sup>4</sup>(11π + θ)) − 2(sin<sup>6</sup>(3π/2 − θ) + sin<sup>6</sup>(9π − θ)), θ ∈ R. Then α + 2β is equal to :
steps: Reducing the angles, the fourth and sixth powers give sin<sup>4</sup>(7π/2 − θ) = cos<sup>4</sup>θ, sin<sup>4</sup>(11π + θ) = sin<sup>4</sup>θ, sin<sup>6</sup>(3π/2 − θ) = cos<sup>6</sup>θ, sin<sup>6</sup>(9π − θ) = sin<sup>6</sup>θ.
With t = sin<sup>2</sup>θ cos<sup>2</sup>θ: sin<sup>4</sup> + cos<sup>4</sup> = 1 − 2t and sin<sup>6</sup> + cos<sup>6</sup> = 1 − 3t, so f = 4(1 − 2t) − 2(1 − 3t) = 2 − 2t.
Since t lies in [0, 1/4], α = 2 and β = 3/2, so α + 2β = 5.

qs.stem: Let a = −i + j + 2k, b = i − j − 3k, c = a × b and d = c × a. Then (a − b)·d is equal to :
steps: c = a × b = (−1, −1, 0).
d = c × a = (−1, −1, 0) × (−1, 1, 2) = (−2, 2, −2).
a − b = (−2, 2, 5), so the dot product is 4 + 4 − 10 = −2.

qs.stem: A building construction work can be completed by two masons A and B together in 22.5 days. Mason A alone can complete the construction work in 24 days less than mason B alone. Then mason A alone will complete the construction work in :
steps: Let A take x days, so B takes x + 24 days. Then 1/x + 1/(x + 24) = 1/22.5 = 2/45.
Cross-multiplying: 45(2x + 24) = 2x(x + 24), giving x<sup>2</sup> − 21x − 540 = 0.
The discriminant is 2601 = 51<sup>2</sup>, so x = (21 + 51)/2 = 36 days.

qs.stem: Let f(x) = (ax<sup>2</sup> + 2ax + 3)/(4x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 3) for x ≠ −3/2, 1/2, and f(x) = b for x = −3/2, 1/2, be continuous at x = −3/2. If fof(x) = 7/5, then x is equal to :
steps: The denominator is (2x + 3)(2x − 1); for the limit at x = −3/2 to exist the numerator must vanish there: 9a/4 − 3a + 3 = 0, so a = 4.
The numerator is then (2x + 1)(2x + 3), so f(x) = (2x + 1)/(2x − 1) elsewhere, and b = limit = (−2)/(−4) = 1/2.
Put y = f(x): (2y + 1)/(2y − 1) = 7/5 gives y = 3. Then (2x + 1)/(2x − 1) = 3 gives x = 1.

qs.stem: The sum of all possible values of n ∈ N, so that the coefficients of x, x<sup>2</sup> and x<sup>3</sup> in the expansion of (1 + x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>(1 + x)<sup>n</sup>, are in arithmetic progression is :
steps: Write (1 + 2x<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>4</sup>)(1 + x)<sup>n</sup>. Coefficients: of x is n, of x<sup>2</sup> is C(n,2) + 2, of x<sup>3</sup> is C(n,3) + 2n.
AP condition: 2(C(n,2) + 2) = n + C(n,3) + 2n, which simplifies to n<sup>3</sup> − 9n<sup>2</sup> + 26n − 24 = 0.
This factors as (n − 2)(n − 3)(n − 4) = 0, so the values are 2, 3, 4 with sum 9.

qs.stem: The value of <sup>100</sup>C<sub>50</sub>/51 + <sup>100</sup>C<sub>51</sub>/52 + … + <sup>100</sup>C<sub>100</sub>/101 is :
steps: The binomial coefficients of 101 are symmetric, so the terms from 51 to 101 total half of 2<sup>101</sup>, i.e. 2<sup>100</sup>. The value is 2<sup>100</sup>/101.

qs.stem: Let the domain of the function f(x) = log<sub>3</sub> log<sub>5</sub> log<sub>7</sub>(9x − x<sup>2</sup> − 13) be the interval (m, n). Let the hyperbola x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1 have eccentricity n/3 and the length of the latus rectum 8m/3. Then b<sup>2</sup> − a<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Domain: log<sub>5</sub> log<sub>7</sub>(·) > 0 requires log<sub>7</sub>(·) > 1, i.e. 9x − x<sup>2</sup> − 13 > 7, so x<sup>2</sup> − 9x + 20 < 0 and the domain is (4, 5): m = 4, n = 5.
Eccentricity 5/3 gives b<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> = 25/9 − 1 = 16/9. Latus rectum 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 32/3 gives 2(16/9)a = 32/3, so a = 3 and b = 4.
b<sup>2</sup> − a<sup>2</sup> = 16 − 9 = 7.

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x<sup>4</sup> dy + (4x<sup>3</sup>y + 2 sin x) dx = 0, x > 0, y(π/2) = 0. Then π<sup>4</sup> y(π/3) is equal to :
steps: The equation reads d(x<sup>4</sup>y) = −2 sin x dx, so x<sup>4</sup>y = 2 cos x + C.
With y(π/2) = 0: 0 = 0 + C, so C = 0 and x<sup>4</sup>y = 2 cos x.
At x = π/3: (π<sup>4</sup>/81) y = 2 · 1/2 = 1, so π<sup>4</sup>y = 81.

qs.stem: Let the direction cosines of two lines satisfy the equations : 4l + m − n = 0 and 2mn + 10nl + 3lm = 0. Then the cosine of the acute angle between these lines is :
steps: From the first, n = 4l + m. Substituting: (4l + m)(2m + 10l) + 3lm = 0, i.e. 2m<sup>2</sup> + 21lm + 40l<sup>2</sup> = 0, so m/l = −8 or −5/2.
Direction ratios: (1, −8, −4) and (2, −5, 3) (check n = 4l + m for each).
Dot product = 2 + 40 − 12 = 30; magnitudes 9 and √38. cos θ = 30/(9√38) = 10/(3√38).

qs.stem: Let the mean and variance of 8 numbers −10, −7, −1, x, y, 9, 2, 16 be 7/2 and 293/4, respectively. Then the mean of 4 numbers x, y, x + y + 1, |x − y| is :
steps: Sum = 8 × 7/2 = 28; the known numbers add to 9, so x + y = 19.
Variance gives ∑x<sup>2</sup>/8 = 293/4 + 49/4 = 171/2, so ∑x<sup>2</sup> = 684; the known squares add to 491, so x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 193.
Then (x − y)<sup>2</sup> = 2(193) − 361 = 25, so |x − y| = 5. Mean = (19 + 20 + 5)/4 = 11.

qs.stem: Let the line y − x = 1 intersect the ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/2 + y<sup>2</sup>/1 = 1 at the points A and B. Then the angle made by the line segment AB at the center of the ellipse is :
steps: Substituting y = x + 1: x<sup>2</sup> + 2(x + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 2, so 3x<sup>2</sup> + 4x = 0; A = (0, 1), B = (−4/3, −1/3).
At the centre O: OA = (0, 1), OB = (−4/3, −1/3), so cos θ = (−1/3)/(√17/3) = −1/√17.
So θ = π − tan<sup>−1</sup>4 = π − (π/2 − tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/4)) = π/2 + tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/4).

qs.stem: Among the statements : I : If det[[1, cosα, cosβ], [cosα, 1, cosγ], [cosβ, cosγ, 1]] = det[[0, cosα, cosβ], [cosα, 0, cosγ], [cosβ, cosγ, 0]], then cos<sup>2</sup>α + cos<sup>2</sup>β + cos<sup>2</sup>γ = 3/2 and II : If det[[x<sup>2</sup> + x, x + 1, x − 2], [2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 1, 3x, 3x − 3], [x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 3, 2x − 1, 2x − 1]] = px + q then p<sup>2</sup> = 196 q<sup>2</sup>.
steps: I: left determinant = 1 − (cos<sup>2</sup>α + cos<sup>2</sup>β + cos<sup>2</sup>γ) + 2 cosα cosβ cosγ; right determinant = 2 cosα cosβ cosγ. Equality gives the sum of squares = 1, not 3/2, so I is false.
II: expanding the determinant gives 24x − 12, so p = 24, q = −12.
p<sup>2</sup> = 576 = 4q<sup>2</sup>, not 196q<sup>2</sup>, so II is false. Both are false.

qs.stem: Let f(x) = ∫ (2 − x<sup>2</sup>)·e<sup>x</sup> / ((√(1 + x))(1 − x)<sup>3/2</sup>) dx. If f(0) = 0, then f(1/2) is equal to :
steps: Try g(x) = e<sup>x</sup>√((1 + x)/(1 − x)). Then g'(x) = e<sup>x</sup>[√((1 + x)/(1 − x)) + 1/((1 + x)<sup>1/2</sup>(1 − x)<sup>3/2</sup>)] = e<sup>x</sup>[(1 − x<sup>2</sup>) + 1]/((1 + x)<sup>1/2</sup>(1 − x)<sup>3/2</sup>), which is the integrand.
So f(x) = e<sup>x</sup>√((1 + x)/(1 − x)) + C, and f(0) = 0 gives C = −1.
f(1/2) = √e · √3 − 1 = √(3e) − 1.

qs.stem: The value of the integral ∫ from π/24 to 5π/24 of dx/(1 + (tan 2x)<sup>1/3</sup>) is :
steps: The limits add to π/4. Replace x by π/4 − x: tan 2(π/4 − x) = cot 2x, so the integrand becomes 1/(1 + (cot 2x)<sup>1/3</sup>) = (tan 2x)<sup>1/3</sup>/(1 + (tan 2x)<sup>1/3</sup>).
Adding the two forms gives 1, so 2I = 5π/24 − π/24 = π/6.

qs.stem: If α and β (α < β) are the roots of the equation (−2 + √3)(|√x − 3|) + (x − 6√x) + (9 − 2√3) = 0, x ≥ 0, then √(β/α) + √(αβ) is equal to :
steps: Let t = √x and u = |t − 3|. Then x − 6√x + 9 = u<sup>2</sup>, and the equation becomes u<sup>2</sup> − (2 − √3)u − 2√3 = 0.
Its roots are u = 2 and u = −√3 (rejected, as u ≥ 0). So |t − 3| = 2, t = 1 or 5, x = 1 or 25.
α = 1, β = 25: √25 + √25 = 10.

qs.stem: The vertices B and C of a triangle ABC lie on the line x/1 = (1 − y)/(−2) = (z − 2)/3. The coordinates of A and B are (1, 6, 3) and (4, 9, α) respectively and C is at a distance of 10 units from B. The area (in sq. units) of ΔABC is :
steps: The line is x = (y − 1)/2 = (z − 2)/3, with direction d = (1, 2, 3) and passing through (0, 1, 2). B(4, 9, α) fits with parameter 4, so α = 14.
BA = (−3, −3, −11); BA × d = (13, −2, −3), of magnitude √182. Height from A to the line = √182/√14 = √13.
Area = (1/2) × BC × height = (1/2)(10)(√13) = 5√13.

qs.stem: Let A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. Let R be a relation on A defined by xRy if and only if 2x + y ≤ 2. Let l be the number of elements in R. Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations respectively. Then l + m + n is equal to :
steps: Count pairs with 2x + y ≤ 2: x = −2 gives 7, x = −1 gives 7, x = 0 gives 5, x = 1 gives 3, x = 2 gives 1, x = 3, 4 give 0. So l = 23.
Reflexive needs 3x ≤ 2; the diagonal pairs missing are for x = 1, 2, 3, 4, so m = 4.
Symmetric: count pairs (x, y) in R with 2y + x > 2 (reverse missing): x = −2 gives y = 3, 4 (2); x = −1 gives y = 2, 3, 4 (3); x = 0 gives y = 2 (1); others 0. So n = 6, and l + m + n = 33.

qs.stem: Let S = {z : 3 ≤ |2z − 3(1 + i)| ≤ 7} be a set of complex numbers. Then the minimum over z ∈ S of |z + (1/2)(5 + 3i)| is equal to :
steps: Dividing by 2: 3/2 ≤ |z − (3/2)(1 + i)| ≤ 7/2, an annulus centred at C(3/2, 3/2).
The expression is the distance from z to P(−5/2, −3/2). CP = |(4, 3)| = 5, which exceeds the outer radius 7/2.
The nearest point of S lies on the outer circle, so the minimum is 5 − 7/2 = 3/2.

qs.stem: Number of solutions of √3 cos 2θ + 8 cos θ + 3√3 = 0, θ ∈ [−3π, 2π] is :
steps: Using cos 2θ = 2cos<sup>2</sup>θ − 1: √3 cos<sup>2</sup>θ + 4 cos θ + √3 = 0, so cos θ = −1/√3 or −√3 (impossible).
cos θ = −1/√3 ≈ −0.577 has 2 solutions in each 2π period, at θ ≈ ±2.186 + 2nπ.
In [−3π, 2π] (length 5π) these are −8.47, −4.10, −2.19, 2.19, 4.10: five solutions.

qs.stem: The number of 4-letter words, with or without meaning, which can be formed using the letters PQRPQRSTUVP, is ________.
steps: Letters available: P × 3, Q × 2, R × 2, and S, T, U, V once each (8 distinct kinds).

Case by pattern: all distinct (choose 4 of 7 kinds in order, with P, Q, R, S, T, U, V) = 7×6×5×4 = 840; one repeated pair + two distinct: 3 choices of pair, C(6,2) other kinds, 4!/2! arrangements = 3×15×12 = 540; two pairs: C(3,2) × 4!/(2!2!) = 18; triple P + one other: 6 × 4 = 24.

qs.stem: Let |A| = 6, where A is a 3 × 3 matrix. If |adj(3 adj(A<sup>2</sup> · adj(2A)))| = 2<sup>m</sup> · 3<sup>n</sup>, m, n ∈ N, then m + n is equal to ________.
steps: adj(2A) = 4 adj A, so A<sup>2</sup>adj(2A) = 4A(A adj A) = 4|A|A = 24A. Then adj(24A) = 576 adj A and M = 3 adj(24A) = 1728 adj A.
For a 3 × 3 matrix |adj M| = |M|<sup>2</sup>, and |M| = 1728<sup>3</sup>|adj A| = 1728<sup>3</sup>·36 = 2<sup>20</sup>·3<sup>11</sup>.
So |adj M| = 2<sup>40</sup>·3<sup>22</sup>, giving m + n = 62.

qs.stem: Let f be a twice differentiable non-negative function such that (f(x))<sup>2</sup> = 25 + ∫ from 0 to x of ((f(t))<sup>2</sup> + (f'(t))<sup>2</sup>) dt. Then the mean of f(log<sub>e</sub>(1)), f(log<sub>e</sub>(2)), …, f(log<sub>e</sub>(625)) is equal to ________.
steps: Differentiate: 2ff' = f<sup>2</sup> + f'<sup>2</sup>, so (f − f')<sup>2</sup> = 0 and f' = f; hence f = Ce<sup>x</sup>.
f(0)<sup>2</sup> = 25 and f ≥ 0 give C = 5, so f(ln k) = 5k.
Mean of 5k for k = 1 to 625 = 5 × (626/2) = 5 × 313 = 1565.

qs.stem: From the first 100 natural numbers, two numbers first a and then b are selected randomly without replacement. If the probability that a − b ≥ 10 is m/n, gcd(m, n) = 1, then m + n is equal to ________.
steps: Ordered pairs (a, b) with a − b = d (10 ≤ d ≤ 99) number 100 − d, so the favourable count is 1 + 2 + … + 90 = 4095.
Total ordered selections = 100 × 99 = 9900.

qs.stem: Let the area of the region bounded by the curve y = max{sin x, cos x}, lines x = 0, x = 3π/2, and the x-axis be A. Then, A + A<sup>2</sup> is equal to ________.
steps: The maximum is cos x on [0, π/4] and sin x on [π/4, 5π/4], then cos x on [5π/4, 3π/2].

Areas (absolute): ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>π/4</sup> cos x = √2/2; ∫<sub>π/4</sub><sup>π</sup> sin x = 1 + √2/2; on [π, 5π/4] sin x is negative, area 1 − √2/2; on [5π/4, 3π/2] cos x is negative, area 1 − √2/2.

qs.stem: Four persons measure the length of a rod as 20.00 cm, 19.75 cm, 17.01 cm and 18.25 cm. The relative error in the measurement of average length of the rod is :
steps: Absolute deviations from the mean: 1.25, 1.00, 1.74, 0.50 cm; their average is 4.49/4 ≈ 1.12 cm.
Relative error = 1.12/18.75 ≈ 0.06.

qs.stem: Two small balls with masses m and 2m are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length d and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is L about an axis (A) passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about A is :
steps: About the centre of mass the moment of inertia of a two-body system is μd<sup>2</sup> with μ = (m × 2m)/(m + 2m) = 2m/3.
So I = (2/3)md<sup>2</sup> and L = Iω.
ω = L/I = 3L/(2md<sup>2</sup>).

qs.stem: A 20 m long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>) through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.5 Gauss perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travels a vertical distance of 200 m is ________ mV.
steps: Speed after falling 200 m from rest: v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 200) = 20√10 m/s.
B = 0.5 G = 0.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup> T, and the field, velocity and wire are mutually perpendicular.
emf = Bvl = 0.5 × 10<sup>−4</sup> × 20√10 × 20 = 20√10 × 10<sup>−3</sup> V = 20√10 mV.

qs.stem: In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies 3 divisions above the horizontal pitch line when their metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument thickness of a sheet is measured. If pitch scale reading is 1 mm and the circular scale reading is 51 then the correct thickness of the sheet is ______ mm. [Assume least count is 0.01 mm]
steps: Zero of the circular scale is above the reference line, so the zero error is negative: −3 × 0.01 = −0.03 mm.
Observed reading = 1 mm + 51 × 0.01 mm = 1.51 mm.
Correct thickness = observed − (zero error) = 1.51 + 0.03 = 1.54 mm.

qs.stem: A thin prism with angle 5° of refractive index 1.72 is combined with another prism of refractive index 1.9 to produce dispersion without deviation. The angle of second prism is ________.
steps: Deviation without dispersion for the mean ray requires the two deviations to cancel: (μ<sub>1</sub> − 1)A<sub>1</sub> = (μ<sub>2</sub> − 1)A<sub>2</sub>.
0.72 × 5° = 0.9 × A<sub>2</sub>.

qs.stem: An object is projected with kinetic energy K from a point A at an angle 60° with the horizontal. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points B and C to that at point A (see figure), in the absence of air friction is :
steps: A and C are at the same height, so KE<sub>C</sub> = KE<sub>A</sub> = K.
At the top B only the horizontal component survives: KE<sub>B</sub> = K cos<sup>2</sup>60° = K/4.
(KE<sub>C</sub> − KE<sub>B</sub>)/KE<sub>A</sub> = (K − K/4)/K = 3/4.

qs.stem: Consider light travelling from a medium A to medium B separated by a plane interface. If the light undergoes total internal reflection during its travel from medium A to B and the speed of light in media A and B are 2.4 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s and 2.7 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s, respectively, then the value of critical angle is :
steps: sin θ<sub>c</sub> = n<sub>B</sub>/n<sub>A</sub> = v<sub>A</sub>/v<sub>B</sub> = 2.4/2.7 = 8/9.
Then cos θ<sub>c</sub> = √(81 − 64)/9 = √17/9.
tan θ<sub>c</sub> = 8/√17, so θ<sub>c</sub> = tan<sup>−1</sup>(8/√17).

qs.stem: A small bob A of mass m is attached to a massless rigid rod of length 1 m pivoted at point P and kept at an angle of 60° with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of 1 m below point P, an identical bob B is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius R as shown in figure. If bob B just manages to complete the circular path of radius R upto a point Q after being hit elastically by bob A, then radius R is ________ m.
steps: Speed of A at the bottom: (1/2)mv<sup>2</sup> = mgL(1 − cos 60°) gives v<sup>2</sup> = gL = 10, so v = √10 m/s.
Elastic collision of equal masses exchanges velocities, so B leaves with √10 m/s.
To just complete a vertical circle at its lowest point, v<sup>2</sup> = 5gR, so 10 = 50R and R = 1/5 m.

qs.stem: A simple pendulum of string length 30 cm performs 20 oscillations in 10 s. The length of the string required for the pendulum to perform 40 oscillations in the same time duration is ________ cm. [Assume that the mass of the pendulum remains same.]
steps: Doubling the number of oscillations in the same time halves the period.
Since T ∝ √l, halving T reduces l to one quarter.

qs.stem: A wire of uniform resistance λ Ω/m is bent into a circle of radius r and another piece of wire with length 2r is connected between points A and B (AOB) as shown in figure. The equivalent resistance between points A and B is ________ Ω.
steps: A and B are 90° apart, so the circle splits into two arcs in parallel with the straight wire: minor arc (πr/2)λ, major arc (3πr/2)λ, straight wire 2rλ.
Conductances: 2/(πλr) + 2/(3πλr) + 1/(2λr) = (12 + 4 + 3π)/(6πλr).
R<sub>eq</sub> = 6πλr/(3π + 16).

qs.stem:
Match List – I with List – II.
List – I (Relation): A. ∮ E·dl = −(d/dt) ∫ B·da; B. ∮ B·dl = μ0(I + ε0 dφE/dt); C. ∮ E·da = (1/ε0) ∫v ρ dv; D. ∮ B·dl = μ0I.
List – II (Law): I. Ampere's circuital law; II. Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction; III. Ampere – Maxwell law; IV. Gauss's law of electrostatics.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A has a changing flux producing an electric circulation, so it is Faraday's law (II).
B contains the displacement-current term, so it is the Ampere-Maxwell law (III).
C relates the electric flux to enclosed charge, so it is Gauss's law (IV); D is the steady-current form, Ampere's circuital law (I).
Matching: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

qs.stem: The strain-stress plot for materials A, B, C and D is shown in the figure. Which material has the largest Young's modulus ?
steps: The plot has strain on the vertical axis and stress on the horizontal axis, so the slope is strain/stress = 1/Y.
Young's modulus Y = 1/slope, so the flattest line has the largest Y.
Line C is the least steep, so material C has the largest Young's modulus.

qs.stem: Two blocks with masses 100 g and 200 g are attached to the ends of springs A and B as shown in figure. The energy stored in A is E. The energy stored in B, when spring constants k<sub>A</sub>, k<sub>B</sub> of A and B, respectively satisfy the relation 4k<sub>A</sub> = 3k<sub>B</sub>, is :
steps: At equilibrium kx = mg, so the stored energy is (1/2)kx<sup>2</sup> = m<sup>2</sup>g<sup>2</sup>/(2k).
E<sub>B</sub>/E<sub>A</sub> = (2m)<sup>2</sup>/m<sup>2</sup> × (k<sub>A</sub>/k<sub>B</sub>) = 4 × (3/4) = 3.
E<sub>B</sub> = 3E.

qs.stem: The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius R and length L (R < L) about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as M) :
steps: Each cylinder has mass M/4. The axis lies in the loop's plane and passes through the middles of two opposite cylinders, perpendicular to them.
Those two: I = (M/4)(R<sup>2</sup>/4 + L<sup>2</sup>/12) each. The other two lie parallel to the axis at distance L/2: I = (M/4)(R<sup>2</sup>/2 + L<sup>2</sup>/4) each.
Total = (M/2)(R<sup>2</sup>/4 + R<sup>2</sup>/2 + L<sup>2</sup>/12 + L<sup>2</sup>/4) = (M/2)(3R<sup>2</sup>/4 + L<sup>2</sup>/3) = (3/8)MR<sup>2</sup> + (1/6)ML<sup>2</sup>.

qs.stem: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of 10 m/s and 30 m/s, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in °C), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is : (specific heat of sphere material 31 cal/kg.°C and 1 cal = 4.2 J)
steps: Common velocity: (25 × 30 − 15 × 10)/40 = 15 m/s.

qs.stem: Two point charges 2q and q are placed at vertex A and centre of face CDEF of the cube as shown in figure. The electric flux passing through the cube is :
steps: A charge at a vertex of a cube sends one eighth of its total flux through the cube: (2q/ε<sub>0</sub>)/8 = q/(4ε<sub>0</sub>).
A charge at the centre of a face sends half of its flux inside: (q/ε<sub>0</sub>)/2 = q/(2ε<sub>0</sub>).
Total flux = q/(4ε<sub>0</sub>) + q/(2ε<sub>0</sub>) = 3q/(4ε<sub>0</sub>).

qs.stem: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Consider a ferromagnetic material : Assertion (A) : The individual atoms in a ferromagnetic material possess a magnetic dipole moment and interact with one another in such a way that they spontaneously align themselves forming domains. Reason (R) : At high enough temperature, the domain structure of ferromagnetic material disintegrates. Thus, magnetization will disappear at high enough temperature known as Curie temperature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: (A) is true: interaction between atomic dipoles makes them align spontaneously within domains.
(R) is also true: above the Curie temperature thermal agitation destroys domains and the material turns paramagnetic.
But the loss of order at high temperature does not explain why domains form in the first place, so (R) is not the explanation of (A).
opts: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

qs.stem: The de Broglie wavelength of an oxygen molecule at 27°C is x × 10<sup>−12</sup> m. The value of x is (take Planck's constant = 6.63 × 10<sup>−34</sup> J.s, Boltzmann constant = 1.38 × 10<sup>−23</sup> J/K, mass of oxygen molecule = 5.31 × 10<sup>−26</sup> kg)
steps: Average thermal kinetic energy (3/2)kT = p<sup>2</sup>/(2m), so p = √(3mkT) and λ = h/√(3mkT).
3mkT = 3 × 5.31 × 10<sup>−26</sup> × 1.38 × 10<sup>−23</sup> × 300 ≈ 6.6 × 10<sup>−46</sup>, whose root is ≈ 2.57 × 10<sup>−23</sup>.
λ = 6.63 × 10<sup>−34</sup>/2.57 × 10<sup>−23</sup> ≈ 25.8 × 10<sup>−12</sup> m, so x ≈ 26.

qs.stem: In hydrogen atom spectrum, (R → Rydberg's constant) (A) the maximum wavelength of the radiation of Lyman series is 4/(3R). (B) the Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum. (C) the minimum wavelength of the radiation of Paschen series is 9/R. (D) the minimum wavelength of Lyman series is 5/(4R). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Longest Lyman wavelength is for 2 → 1: 1/λ = R(1 − 1/4) = 3R/4, so λ = 4/(3R): (A) true.
Balmer lines (about 656 to 365 nm, mainly visible): (B) true.
Shortest Paschen wavelength is for ∞ → 3: 1/λ = R/9, so λ = 9/R: (C) true.
Shortest Lyman wavelength is 1/R, not 5/(4R): (D) false. So A, B and C.

qs.stem: In two separate Young's double-slit experimental set-ups and two monochromatic light sources of different wavelengths are used to get fringes of equal width. The ratios of the slits separations and that of the wavelengths of light used are 2 : 1 and 1 : 2 respectively. The corresponding ratio of the distances between the slits and the respective screens (D<sub>1</sub>/D<sub>2</sub>) is ________.
steps: Fringe width β = λD/d, and the two widths are equal.
D<sub>1</sub>/D<sub>2</sub> = (λ<sub>2</sub>/λ<sub>1</sub>)(d<sub>1</sub>/d<sub>2</sub>).

qs.stem: The space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C (without any dielectric) is now filled with three dielectric slabs of dielectric constants K<sub>1</sub> = 2, K<sub>2</sub> = 3 and K<sub>3</sub> = 5 (as shown in figure). If new capacitance is (n/3)C then the value of n is ________.
steps: Slab K<sub>1</sub> (thickness d/2, full area A) has capacitance 2 × 2C = 4C. Slabs K<sub>2</sub> and K<sub>3</sub> (thickness d/2, area A/2 each) have 3C and 5C, in parallel: 8C.
This 8C is in series with 4C: C<sub>eq</sub> = (4C × 8C)/(12C) = 8C/3.
Comparing with nC/3 gives n = 8.
qs.fig: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 130' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='20' y1='30' x2='180' y2='30' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='20' y1='100' x2='180' y2='100' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='3'/><line x1='20' y1='65' x2='180' y2='65' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='100' y1='65' x2='100' y2='100' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='20' y1='30' x2='20' y2='100' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='180' y1='30' x2='180' y2='100' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1'/><text x='95' y='52' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>K1</text><text x='55' y='88' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>K2</text><text x='135' y='88' font-size='12' fill='currentColor'>K3</text><text x='186' y='50' font-size='9' fill='currentColor'>d/2</text><text x='186' y='86' font-size='9' fill='currentColor'>d/2</text><text x='60' y='22' font-size='9' fill='currentColor'>area A (top plate, +)</text><text x='60' y='116' font-size='9' fill='currentColor'>K2: A/2, K3: A/2 (bottom plate, −)</text></svg>

qs.stem: Using a variable frequency a.c. voltage source the maximum current measured in the given LCR circuit is 50 mA for V = 5 sin(100t). The values of L and R are shown in the figure (L = 2 H, R = 100 Ω, series circuit). The capacitance of the capacitor (C) used is ________ μF.
steps: Peak current 50 mA with peak voltage 5 V means Z = 5/0.05 = 100 Ω = R.
Impedance equals R only at resonance, so X<sub>L</sub> = X<sub>C</sub> at ω = 100 rad/s.
X<sub>L</sub> = ωL = 200 Ω, so C = 1/(ωX<sub>C</sub>) = 1/(100 × 200) = 5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> F = 50 μF.

qs.stem: The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : E = √377 sin(6.27 × 10<sup>3</sup>t − 2.09 × 10<sup>−5</sup>x) N/C. The average power of the electromagnetic wave is (1/α) W/m<sup>2</sup>. The value of α is ________. (Take √(μ<sub>0</sub>/ε<sub>0</sub>) = 377 in SI units)
steps: Average intensity I = (1/2)ε<sub>0</sub>E<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>c, with E<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> = 377.
Since √(μ<sub>0</sub>/ε<sub>0</sub>) = μ<sub>0</sub>c = 377, we get ε<sub>0</sub>c = 1/377.

qs.stem: A simple pendulum made of mass 10 g and a metallic wire of length 10 cm is suspended vertically in a uniform magnetic field of 2 T. The magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of oscillations of the pendulum. If the pendulum is released from an angle of 60° with vertical, then maximum induced EMF between the point of suspension and point of oscillation is ________ mV. (Take g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Speed at the lowest point: v = √(2gl(1 − cos 60°)) = √(gl) = √(10 × 0.1) = 1 m/s.
Maximum EMF between the ends of a rod rotating about one end is (1/2)Bωl<sup>2</sup> = (1/2)Bvl (with v = ωl the tip speed).
EMF = 0.5 × 2 × 1 × 0.1 = 0.1 V = 100 mV.

qs.stem: Consider the following sequence of reactions: 4-nitrotoluene → [(i) Sn, HCl/Δ; (ii) pH neutralisation] (A) → [(i) (H<sub>3</sub>CCO)<sub>2</sub>O; (ii) Br<sub>2</sub>/AcOH] (B). Assuming that the reaction proceeds to completion, then 137 mg of 4-nitrotoluene will produce _____ mg of B. (Given molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup>: H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, Br : 80)
steps: Sn/HCl reduces the nitro group: A = 4-methylaniline. Acetic anhydride then gives the acetanilide, and Br<sub>2</sub>/AcOH brominates ortho to the NHCOCH<sub>3</sub> group: B = N-(2-bromo-4-methylphenyl)acetamide, C<sub>9</sub>H<sub>10</sub>BrNO.
Moles of 4-nitrotoluene (M = 137) = 137 mg / 137 = 1 mmol, and the conversion is 1:1.
M of B = 9(12) + 10 + 80 + 14 + 16 = 228 g/mol, so mass of B = 1 mmol × 228 = 228 mg.

qs.stem: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the 3<sup>rd</sup> period of periodic table is :
steps: Across period 3 the first IE rises overall, with two dips: Mg > Al (3p electron is easier to remove) and P > S (half-filled 3p<sup>3</sup> of P is stable).
Values (kJ/mol): Al 578, Si 786, S 1000, P 1012, Cl 1251.
Order among the options: Al < Si < S < P < Cl.

qs.stem: 'x' is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. 'y' is the product which is obtained from the but–2–ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of 'x' and one mole of 'y' react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating ?
steps: SnCl<sub>2</sub>/HCl (Stephen reduction) turns CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CN into propanal (x). Ozonolysis of but-2-ene gives 2 CH<sub>3</sub>CHO, so y = ethanal.

With alkali the mixture undergoes aldol condensations: ethanal + ethanal gives but-2-enal; propanal enolate + ethanal gives 2-methylbut-2-enal; ethanal enolate + propanal gives pent-2-enal; propanal + propanal gives 2-methylpent-2-enal.
3-Methylbut-2-enal, (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>C=CHCHO, would need a ketone or a branched carbon-3 skeleton that cannot be formed from these two aldehydes, so it is not obtained.

qs.stem: But–2–yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq. NH<sub>3</sub> to give the products X and Y respectively. Identify the incorrect statements : A. X and Y are stereoisomers. B. Dipole moment of X is zero. C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y. D. X and Y react with O<sub>3</sub>/Zn + H<sub>2</sub>O to give different products. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: The question treats Pd/C with H<sub>2</sub> as syn addition, so X = cis-but-2-ene, while Na/liq. NH<sub>3</sub> gives anti addition, so Y = trans-but-2-ene. They are geometric isomers: A is true.
cis-But-2-ene has a net dipole moment, so B (zero dipole) is false; the cis isomer is polar and boils higher (about 4 °C vs 1 °C), so C is true.
Both isomers on ozonolysis give 2 CH<sub>3</sub>CHO, the same product, so D is false. Incorrect statements: B and D.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point. Statement II : The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Sublimation purifies solids that pass directly to vapour on heating; such compounds do not have to be low melting, so Statement I is false.
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external pressure. Reducing external pressure lowers the boiling point (the basis of vacuum distillation), so Statement II is false.
Both are false.
opts: Statement I is false but statement II is true.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.
Both statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but statement II is false.

qs.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Functional group, detection): A. Unsaturation (Baeyer's test); B. Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test); C. Aldehyde group (Tollen's reagent); D. Phenolic group (FeCl<sub>3</sub> test). List-II (Change observed during detection): I. Red colour appears; II. Silver mirror appears; III. Violet colour appears; IV. Discharge of pink colour. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Baeyer's reagent (cold dilute alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub>) is decolourised by a C=C or C≡C bond: A → IV (pink colour discharged).
Ceric ammonium nitrate turns yellow solution red with alcohols: B → I.
Aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent to a silver mirror: C → II. Phenols give a violet complex with neutral FeCl<sub>3</sub>: D → III.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements : Statement I : [CoBr4]2− ion will absorb light of lower energy than [CoCl4]2− ion. Statement II : In [CoI4]2− ion, the energy separation between the two set of d–orbitals is more than [CoCl4]2− ion. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Spectrochemical series: Cl<sup>−</sup> > Br<sup>−</sup> > I<sup>−</sup>, so the tetrahedral splitting Δ<sub>t</sub> follows [CoCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> > [CoBr<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> > [CoI<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>.
Absorbed energy is proportional to Δ<sub>t</sub>, so the bromo complex absorbs lower-energy light than the chloro one: Statement I is true.
The iodo complex has a smaller, not larger, splitting than the chloro one: Statement II is false.
opts: Both statement I and statement II are false.
Statement I is false but statement II is true.
Statement I is true but statement II is false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.

qs.stem: The correct statements from the following are : A. Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decreases down the group. B. Electronegativity of group 13 element decreases down the group. C. Among the group 13 elements, Boron has highest first ionisation enthalpy. D. The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A is false: ionic radii of M<sup>3+</sup> increase down the group as more shells are added.
B is false: electronegativity is irregular (Al is lower than Ga), not a steady decrease.

C is true: boron, the smallest, has the highest first IE (801 kJ/mol) in the group. D is true as taken by the paper (small, highly polarising M<sup>3+</sup> with polarisable Cl<sup>−</sup>/I<sup>−</sup> gives covalent halides). Correct: C and D.

qs.stem: In the given electrochemical cell, Ag(s) | AgCl(s) | FeCl<sub>2</sub> (aq), FeCl<sub>3</sub>(aq) | Pt(s) at 298 K, the cell potential (E<sub>cell</sub>) will increase when : A. Concentration of Fe<sup>2+</sup> is increased. B. Concentration of Fe<sup>3+</sup> is decreased. C. Concentration of Fe<sup>2+</sup> is decreased. D. Concentration of Fe<sup>3+</sup> is increased. E. Concentration of Cl<sup>−</sup> is increased. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Anode: Ag + Cl<sup>−</sup> → AgCl + e<sup>−</sup>; cathode (Pt): Fe<sup>3+</sup> + e<sup>−</sup> → Fe<sup>2+</sup>. Net: Ag + Cl<sup>−</sup> + Fe<sup>3+</sup> → AgCl + Fe<sup>2+</sup>.
Q = [Fe<sup>2+</sup>]/([Fe<sup>3+</sup>][Cl<sup>−</sup>]) and E = E° − 0.0591 log Q, so E rises when Q falls.
Q falls when [Fe<sup>2+</sup>] is decreased (C), [Fe<sup>3+</sup>] is increased (D) or [Cl<sup>−</sup>] is increased (E).

qs.stem: Consider the general reaction given below at 400 K. xA(g) ⇌ yB(g). The values of K<sub>p</sub> and K<sub>c</sub> are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in x and y. (i) K<sub>p</sub> = 85.87 and K<sub>c</sub> = 2.586 appropriate units. (ii) K<sub>p</sub> = 0.862 and K<sub>c</sub> = 28.62 appropriate units. The values of x and y in (i) and (ii) respectively are :
steps: K<sub>p</sub> = K<sub>c</sub>(RT)<sup>Δn</sup> with Δn = y − x, and RT = 0.0821 × 400 ≈ 32.8 (or 33.3 with R = 0.0831).
(i) K<sub>p</sub>/K<sub>c</sub> = 85.87/2.586 ≈ 33 ≈ RT, so Δn = +1; among the options only (x, y) = (1, 2) fits.
(ii) K<sub>p</sub>/K<sub>c</sub> = 0.862/28.62 ≈ 0.030 ≈ 1/RT, so Δn = −1: (x, y) = (2, 1). Answer: (1,2) and (2,1).

qs.stem: Given, (A) n = 5, m<sub>l</sub> = −1 ; (B) n = 3, l = 2, m<sub>l</sub> = −1, m<sub>s</sub> = +1/2. The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) respectively are :
steps: (A) For n = 5 and m<sub>l</sub> = −1, l can be 1, 2, 3 or 4 (l must be at least 1 for m<sub>l</sub> = −1 to exist): four orbitals (5p, 5d, 5f, 5g), each holding 2 electrons: 4 × 2 = 8.
(B) n, l, m<sub>l</sub> fix one orbital and m<sub>s</sub> fixes the spin, so at most 1 electron. Answer: 8 and 1.

qs.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one-electron systems?
steps: E<sub>n</sub> = −2.18 × 10<sup>−18</sup> × Z<sup>2</sup>/n<sup>2</sup> J, always negative for bound states, so options (1) and (3) are wrong.
Li<sup>2+</sup>, n = 3: Z<sup>2</sup>/n<sup>2</sup> = 9/9 = 1, so E = −2.18 × 10<sup>−18</sup> J: option (2) is correct.
H, n = 2: E = −2.18 × 10<sup>−18</sup>/4 = −5.45 × 10<sup>−19</sup> J, not −1.09 × 10<sup>−18</sup>: option (4) is wrong.
opts: +8.72×10<sup>−18</sup> J for first orbit of He<sup>+</sup> ion
−2.18×10<sup>−18</sup> J or third orbit of Li<sup>2+</sup> ion
+2.18×10<sup>−18</sup> J for second orbit of He<sup>+</sup> ion
−1.09×10<sup>−18</sup> J for second orbit of H atom.

qs.stem: The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are : A. It is red in colour. B. It has a high solubility in water at pH = 9. C. The Ni ion has two unpaired d-electrons. D. The N – Ni – N bond angle is almost close to 90°. E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles (metal containing rings). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: [Ni(dmg)<sub>2</sub>] is a bright rosy-red, water-insoluble precipitate formed in ammoniacal (basic) medium, so A is correct and B (high solubility) is incorrect.
Ni<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>8</sup>) with strong-field N donors is square planar and diamagnetic, so C (two unpaired electrons) is incorrect.
Square planar geometry gives N–Ni–N angles close to 90° (D correct). Each dmg ligand forms one five-membered chelate ring, so the complex has two rings, not four: E is incorrect. Incorrect: B, C, E.

qs.stem: Identify the molecule (X) with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons (obtained using Lewis dot structure) among HNO<sub>3</sub>, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>, NF<sub>3</sub> and O<sub>3</sub>. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of the molecule (X).
steps: Count lone pairs: HNO<sub>3</sub> has 7 on its oxygens, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> has 8, O<sub>3</sub> has 6, and NF<sub>3</sub> has 3 × 3 on F plus 1 on N = 10.
So X = NF<sub>3</sub>, with 3 bond pairs and one lone pair on N (pyramidal).
The F–N–F angle is about 102° (smaller than NH<sub>3</sub>'s 107° because the bonding pairs are pulled towards the electronegative F).

qs.stem: Consider all the structural isomers with molecular formula C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>11</sub>Br are separately treated with KOH(aq) to give respective substitution products, without any rearrangement. The number of products which can exhibit optical isomerism from these is _____.
steps: C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>11</sub>Br has 8 structural isomers, giving 8 alcohols (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>11</sub>OH) by substitution: 1-, 2-, 3-pentanol; 2-methylbutan-1-ol; 3-methylbutan-1-ol; 2-methylbutan-2-ol; 3-methylbutan-2-ol; 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol.
Alcohols with a stereocentre: pentan-2-ol, 2-methylbutan-1-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
So 3 products (alcohols) exhibit optical isomerism.

qs.stem: For the following gas phase equilibrium reaction at constant temperature, NH<sub>3</sub>(g) ⇌ 1/2 N<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3/2 H<sub>2</sub>(g), if the total pressure is √3 atm and the pressure equilibrium constant (K<sub>p</sub>) is 9 atm, then the degree of dissociation is given as (x × 10<sup>−2</sup>)<sup>−1/2</sup>. The value of x is ______ (nearest integer)
steps: Start with 1 mol NH<sub>3</sub>: at equilibrium NH<sub>3</sub> = 1 − α, N<sub>2</sub> = α/2, H<sub>2</sub> = 3α/2; total n = 1 + α.
K<sub>p</sub> = [(α/2)<sup>1/2</sup>(3α/2)<sup>3/2</sup>/(1 − α)] × (P/n)<sup>1</sup> = [3<sup>3/2</sup>α<sup>2</sup>/(4(1 − α))] × √3/(1 + α) = 9α<sup>2</sup>/(4(1 − α<sup>2</sup>)).
Set equal to 9: α<sup>2</sup>/(1 − α<sup>2</sup>) = 4, so α<sup>2</sup> = 0.8.
α = 0.8<sup>1/2</sup> = (1.25)<sup>−1/2</sup> = (125 × 10<sup>−2</sup>)<sup>−1/2</sup>, so x = 125.

qs.stem: The crystal field splitting energy of [Co(oxalate)<sub>3</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> complex is 'n' times that of the [Cr(oxalate)<sub>3</sub>]<sup>−3</sup> complex. Here 'n' is______. (Assume Δ<sub>0</sub> >> P)
steps: Both are octahedral with the same ligand, and Δ<sub>0</sub> is assumed equal; the comparison is of crystal field stabilisation energy in units of Δ<sub>0</sub>.
Co<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>6</sup>; with Δ<sub>0</sub> >> P it is low spin t<sub>2g</sub><sup>6</sup>e<sub>g</sub><sup>0</sup>: CFSE = 6(−0.4) = −2.4 Δ<sub>0</sub>.
Cr<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>3</sup>: t<sub>2g</sub><sup>3</sup>: CFSE = 3(−0.4) = −1.2 Δ<sub>0</sub>. Ratio n = 2.4/1.2 = 2.
